group.passage: A QR Code, a quick-response code, is a special kind of barcode made up of a square pattern with black and white squares. QR Code was designed by a Japanese engineer, Masahiro Hara. After completing studies at Hosei University, Hara joined Denso, a subsidiary of the Toyota Group. In 1992, he was assigned to create a new 2D code for tracking automotive components efficiently. Inspired by a game of go during lunch break, Hara realized that its black and white pattern could encode data. He thus conducted research to design optimal position patterns for readability of the code. Finally, he successfully created QR code in 1994, which revolutionized tracking systems. The uses of QR codes vary across different contexts. They provide virtual event access, offer multimedia content, and facilitate mobile shopping experiences. As for shopping, QR codes streamline payments, store bank details securely, and support various digital payment platforms. Take restaurants for example. QR codes make it possible for consumers to view menus, place orders, and make payments without lining up or interacting with staff, which ensures safety during the COVID-19 pandemic, and thus enhances convenience in dining experiences. Other industries also benefit from QR codes. Obviously, the widespread adoption underscores QR codes’ role in modernizing retail and hospitality industries. However, QR codes are not without shortcomings. First, not every smartphone can scan QR codes directly, which sometimes requires users to download additional apps. Second, they rely on the Internet connectivity. Users who are denied Internet access may fail to use them. Third, there is always the risk of personal data being leaked through scanning a seemingly legitimate QR code. Last, QR codes provide one-way communication only, hindering effective interactions, particularly in customer support settings. Despite the drawbacks mentioned above, it is believed that QR code technology will evolve, and its role in advancing technology industry is expected to persist.
